The eval is the only artifact that could decide it, and by its own record a one-scenario gap (30 vs 29) sits inside about two scenarios of producer variance, so the run returns no verdict either way — it neither confirms nor refuses the DOD. Reading that indecisive run as a pass would mean inventing an after-the-fact tolerance ('a one-scenario drop is acceptable'), which the kernel forbids: no numeric threshold may be introduced after start that was not in the admitted DOD, and correcting the DOD to something the evidence can meet is a separate explicit operation requiring a source and a reason, i.e. his word. What remains open is therefore not a buildable result awaiting his glance — the rule that his eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery does not apply — but a genuine fork the artifacts cannot settle: whether 3.7 KB off the pack's front door is worth an unmeasurable and possibly real cost in Director's behaviour. That is one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserves for him. Nothing is committed, so the row stays open with both versions on disk, and the question put to him is which trade he wants; his answer then rides in as the source of a corrected DOD or a decision on the existing row, creating no new work.
